html:
SMTO-BOOT-0021 — No Conda environment with that name was found to check

GUID: 17cd3195-4dba-4eba-9b84-48e7f57342c1
Slug: boot-conda-environment-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • You asked the installer to check an existing Conda environment, the space where the model software is installed, but Conda has none with that exact name. Check-only mode never creates one, so nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run conda env list and find the environment where you installed vLLM. The check needs the exact name; the setup guide uses vllm, but you may have chosen another.
  2. Run the check again with that exact name, for example ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only vllm Names must match exactly, including capital letters, dots and dashes.
  3. If the name isn't listed, compare the "Using Conda:" line in the output with where you installed vLLM, and set CONDA_HOME to that Conda folder. Each Conda installation keeps its own list of environments, so the installer may be looking in the wrong one.
  4. If vLLM was never installed, run the installer without --verify-only to create the environment. Check-only mode doesn't create anything; the normal install does.

What success looks like

  • The installer prints "Checking dependencies, vLLM imports, and CUDA access" and ends with "vLLM verification complete".

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0021 line, the "Using Conda" line and the Error reference line, plus the output of conda env list, and send it to the person who set up vLLM. Don't start a fresh install unless you mean to; it downloads and installs everything again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • install-vllm.sh --verify-only found no environment in conda env list --json of the selected Conda whose directory name exactly matches the requested name.

What this means

  • Verify-only mode queries Conda and finds no environment matching the exact requested name. Verify-only mode reads the Conda environment list and exits without creating an environment or installing packages. The environment might exist under another Conda installation or a different name.

Why this can happen

  • Verify-only mode queries Conda and finds no environment matching the exact requested name.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact name with the selected Conda installation's environment list.

How to fix it

  • Compare the requested name with conda env list for the Conda shown on the installer's 'Using Conda:' line; pass the exact existing name or set CONDA_HOME to the Conda installation that owns the environment. Verify-only never creates environments; run install-vllm.sh without --verify-only to create one.
  • Check the environment list and choose the exact existing name, or create the intended new environment using the installation flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select the intended Conda installation and exact existing environment name before running --verify-only again.

How to verify the fix

  • Verification selects an existing intended environment or a separate deliberate install creates one.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Verify-only mode reads the Conda environment list and exits without creating an environment or installing packages.
  • The environment might exist under another Conda installation or a different name.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
